headline: PSX strings together a second green session as global fear eases, but hot inflation keeps the SBP on hold and today's live breakout signals sit in small, fundamentally shaky names.
summary: PSX closed 175,328.82 (+0.23%), a second straight positive session, helped by a calmer global tape — VIX fell sharply and Brent eased off its highs — even as gold's safe-haven bid persists and the US-Iran/Hormuz conflict stays active. Domestically, August CPI printed a hot 11.1% YoY, all but ruling out a rate cut at the September 14 SBP meeting, and banks, E&P and refiners were still sold on the day. The desk reads this as stabilization inside a risk-off regime, not a turn: favour selective, well-capitalized banks and refiners on weakness, avoid OMCs, autos, cement and small leveraged names, and treat today's technical breakouts with caution given the weak balance sheets underneath.

sectors.name: Banks (large, well-capitalized)
sectors.why: ABL, BAFL, BOP, MCB and NBP all screen 'attractive' on fundamentals (cheap P/E, covered dividends) and the 6M T-bill (11.90%) / 10Y PIB (12.30%) carry tailwind is intact now that 11.1% CPI has taken a Sept 14 rate cut off the table — but banks were sold today, so this is a buy-on-weakness case, not a chase.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: ATRL and NRL both screen 'mixed' but cheap (P/E 4.9x and 7.1x) and still ride the elevated-crude tailwind macro.json flags — refinery names were among today's sold sectors too, so selectivity over a broad bid is the desk's read.

sectors.name: E&P (OGDC/PPL/MARI/POL)
sectors.why: All screen 'mixed' to 'attractive' on fundamentals (POL stands out cheap with a 13.5% yield) and benefit from the Brent shock, but the sector was sold alongside banks today — no fresh trigger to act on, just watching for confirmation.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: Squeezed between a near-daily-reset pump price and a rising import bill, and among the weakest sectors on today's PSX tape per macro.json.

sectors.name: Autos, cement, power/IPPs
sectors.why: Rate-sensitive and import-cost exposed, with power/IPPs also carrying the unresolved circular-debt overhang into the IMF's September review — power generation was among today's sold sectors.

sectors.name: Small/thinly-capitalized banks & broad cyclicals
sectors.why: The confirmed 11.1% CPI print removes any near-term rate-relief thesis, and the active, still-escalating US-Iran/Hormuz conflict argues against chasing broad risk after just two modest up sessions.

watchlist.angle: The Donchian 55 breakout (turtle) triggered today on NRL — 55% win rate over 60 trades, +2.1% net/trade, still profitable out-of-sample (57% oos hit) — the best-sampled signal on the board today, medium confidence. Fundamentals rate 'mixed' but valuation is cheap (P/E 7.1x) in a sector macro.json still tags favoured, selectively.
watchlist.risk: Thin 1.4% net margin and no dividend cushion — refiners were among today's sold sectors, so the setup needs the crude/refining-margin tailwind to hold, not just the chart pattern; no dated catalyst found in the calendar to lean on.

watchlist.angle: Trend + momentum combo triggered today — 58% win rate over 19 trades, +1.3% net/trade, still working out-of-sample (60% oos hit), medium confidence. Results due 2026-09-30 give it a real dated catalyst to watch.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals rate 'caution' — lossmaking (net margin -4.5%), no dividend, small-cap with an above-market beta (1.16). This is a technical-only setup until results prove the story otherwise.

watchlist.angle: Donchian 55 breakout triggered today with the strongest expectancy on the board — 62% win rate over 13 trades (+3.6% net/trade), still profitable out-of-sample (75% oos hit), though the sample is small (low confidence). Results due 2026-09-30 give a dated catalyst.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals rate 'caution' and are weak outright — lossmaking, no dividend, small-cap, beta 1.31 (moves more than the market). A chart to watch, not a balance sheet to lean on.

watchlist.angle: MACD histogram turning up triggered today — 64% win rate over 14 trades (+1.5% net/trade), low confidence — the weakest-sampled of today's four live signals.
watchlist.risk: Fundamentals rate 'caution' too — expensive P/E (14.5x), thin 1.8% net margin, no dividend, and the out-of-sample hit rate is just 40% — the least convincing of today's triggers, and no dated catalyst in the calendar.

catalysts.event: SCBPL book closure — Rs3.0 dividend, 4.74% yield
SBP MPC decision — hawkish hold is the base case after the 11.1% August CPI print

risks: The US-Iran/Strait of Hormuz conflict remains active and escalating — Bloomberg reports oil headed for its biggest weekly gain since July on renewed hostilities even as spot Brent eased today; a re-escalation reverses the calmer tape fast.
Confirmed 11.1% August CPI locks in an extended hawkish SBP stance into the Sept 14 MPC, removing any near-term rate-relief case for banks, autos, cement and leveraged names.
The SECP/FIA fraud-probe escalation at Unity Foods (UNITY, ~Rs44.7bn discrepancy alleged, unconfirmed) is a live governance headline that could dent broader sentiment if it widens.
disclaimer: Research, not advice. The desk generates signals; it does not place orders. Losses are expected.
